summary: Pushkin Lake fire tower in Ben Nevis Township, Cochrane District: a 1949 towerman's cabin is recorded, a 2013-era Ontario list counted it standing, and its state today is unconfirmed.

facts.status_note: Listed as still standing in Ontario's still-standing list, which refers to MNR removal decisions as of 2013. A post calls the tower abandoned, but that post is undated. No source read confirms its condition today.

access.note: The still-standing list says the MNR no longer maintains these towers and asks visitors not to climb them. No source read describes an official access arrangement for this tower.

facts.agency: Ontario Department of Lands and Forests

events.note: The 1949 Report of the Department of Lands and Forests, as quoted by Canada Lookouts, records a frame cabin measuring 22 X 18 erected for a towerman in Ben Nevis Township. The quote does not mention a tower.

Ontario's still-standing list gives the site as Ben Nevis Tower, Pushkin Lake, Kirkland Lake, and does not mark it removed. The list says the MNR had decided, as of 2013, to remove many still-standing towers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Ontario list gives Pushkin Lake, Kirkland Lake. Canada Lookouts places the site at Pushkin Lake in Ben Nevis Township, and Wikipedia places that township in Cochrane District. This record follows the township and lake, and the Kirkland Lake reference is the list's own.

sources.title: Abandoned fire tower west of Pushkin Lake in Ben Nevis Township

notes_for_editor: No source read gives this tower's build date, height or design. The only dated item tied to the site is a 1949 frame cabin for a towerman, which the quote does not link to a tower. The still-standing list is about 2013 and is the only status source for the tower; no date for the Facebook post could be read, and it was readable only as its title, so its abandoned description is unverified. The list's Kirkland Lake reference conflicts with the township sources, and the story follows the township. Brief coordinates (48.293798, -79.693663) fit the post's location about 30 km north of Larder Lake. firelookout.ca and the LIO geohub dataset gave no readable record.
